name: Prestige Estates Projects Ltd
title: Prestige Estates Projects Ltd - 533274 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Prestige Q1 FY27 resi presales INR6,579 crore and collections INR4,802 crore; reported margins softer as handovers fell and launches slipped into Q2/Q3.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a stable start, with resi presales of INR6,579 crore on 337 units and collections of INR4,802 crore. Four launches (about 20.16 million sq ft, roughly INR12,000 crore GDV) were made, led by Prestige Golden Grove in Hyderabad, which was about 60% sold. Reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY because few residential completions meant lower handovers while fixed costs rose ahead of heavy Q2/Q3 launches; management said project-level margins were unchanged. Several Bangalore and Chennai launches slipped from Q1 into Q2/Q3 on approval timing, and the company added three Mumbai JDA/JV sites (Aram Nagar, Thane, Borivali).

financial_highlights.change: Lower due to few major completions in the quarter
EBITDA margin about 41%; PAT contribution about INR419 million
Up from about INR10,900 crore at March (annual report)

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Presales INR6,579 crore; sales split Hyderabad 49%, Bangalore 27%, Mumbai 12%, NCR 7%, other 5%. Four launches with about INR12,000 crore GDV in Q1; FY27 resi collections guided at INR21,000-22,000 crore.

segments.name: Office / commercial annuity
segments.commentary: Gross leasing of 1.5 million sq ft in the quarter; the entire Prestige JRC Signature Tower pre-leased to a leading bank. FY27 exit rental for commercial portfolio stated at INR865 crore.

segments.name: Retail malls
segments.commentary: Gross turnover up 18% YoY to INR737 crore; footfalls 5.2 million in the quarter; FY27 exit rental INR370 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR300 crore in the quarter with about 41% EBITDA margin. IPO approval valid to 30 September; PE interest is being explored as an alternative monetisation route.

guidance_outlook: Gross collections for FY27 near INR25,000 crore, with residential at INR21,000-22,000 crore; the current run rate implies about INR20,000-21,000 crore unless Q2/Q3 launches add cash.
Free cash flow guided at INR8,500-9,000 crore for FY27, enough to fund capex and about INR4,500 crore of business development; net debt may rise by INR1,000-1,500 crore at most.
Business development spend target about INR4,500 crore for FY27.

Launch pipeline of about INR45,000 crore pending; Q2 includes Bangalore (Garden Breez, Avon, Springwood, Battersea) and Chennai Palm Court; Park Street in Chennai in Q2 or Q3; Q3 includes Prestige Meadows (NCR), Bougainvillea Gardens and Chambers 51 (Mumbai).
Residential revenue recognition from the unrecognised backlog of about INR70,000 crore expected over about 4 years; FY27 residential recognition close to INR11,000-12,000 crore.
Management reiterated the 15-20% presales growth guidance from the prior call.
capex_capacity: Four launches in Q1 (Golden Grove, Gardenia Estates Phase 2, Forest Hills Phase 2, Century Landmark commercial); three projects completed (Tech Forest, Sanctuary, Cityscape Kochi) totalling 4.37 million sq ft.
Two annuity projects (Tech Zone and JRC) pushed about 2-3 months, from March 2027 to around June 2027; JRC handover to tenant committed for June quarter FY28.

Chennai pipeline: Palm Court (about INR1,200 crore GDV, Q2), Park Street (about INR1,500 crore, luxury, Q2/Q3), Falcon City (6.84 million sq ft, about INR5,000 crore, Q3), Clover Dale (about 4 million sq ft, about INR5,000 crore, Q4).

NCR: three projects tied up (Sector 150, Prestige Meadows in Sector 92 with INR4,500 crore GDV targeting November launch, and Falcon City). Thane JDA (GDV about INR9,000 crore) registered; Borivali is also a state JDA.
Data centre: about 100 MW envisaged; no land purchased yet, with a Maharashtra government land acquisition pending.
demand_pricing: Hyderabad sales realisation is INR8,000-10,000 per sq ft versus INR14,000-15,000 elsewhere; the Q1 average fell due to the Golden Grove mix. Prestige Place (mixed-use, Marriott and St. Regis branded residences) is planned with a higher price point.
Golden Grove (GDV about INR9,500 crore incl. landowner share, not for sale) is about 60% sold; Hyderabad unsold inventory is about 7 million sq ft out of total 16-17 million sq ft.

Management said demand is intact despite geopolitical and cost pressure; oil and commodity prices raised costs, and labour returned after a roughly two-month disruption during the Assam and West Bengal elections, which may push handovers by about a month.
Approval and RERA delays were the main reason launches slipped; management said each project is at a different approval stage.
Forest Hills Phase 2 launched late in the quarter with limited Q1 sales; Mumbai BKC (X) about 70% leased as of last call; Mahalaxmi about 400,000 sq ft pre-committed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are annuity office revenue projections for FY27 and FY28 lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Two projects (Tech Zone and JRC) slipped about 2-3 months, from March 2027 to around June 2027. JRC is fully pre-leased and handover to the tenant is committed for the June quarter of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q2/Q3 launch pipeline and business development spend stay on target?
qa_highlights.answer: BD target is about INR4,500 crore for FY27, with the balance in Bangalore and Gurgaon. The Q2 Bangalore and Chennai launches depend on approvals that are expected within about 8-10 days for some; the company said some approvals may slip into Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt and free cash flow move through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FCF of INR8,500-9,000 crore is expected to fund capex and BD, with a net debt increase of at most INR1,000-1,500 crore. Q2/Q3 launches should unlock cash and reduce debt on land parcels.

qa_highlights.question: Why is reported EBITDA margin lower despite stable project margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Residential handovers were low because there were no major completions in Q1, while fixed costs rose ahead of heavy Q2/Q3 launches, creating a revenue recognition mismatch. Project-level margins are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the hospitality IPO and monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The IPO approval is valid until 30 September. Management is exploring PE interest and other options and gave no definitive timeline. Hospitality revenue was INR300 crore with about 41% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has an MoU with the Maharashtra government. No land has been acquired or invested yet, and about 100 MW is the planned scale, with the company aiming to invest in land and buildings and partner with data centre operators.

risks_watch: Launch slippage: roughly INR45,000 crore of launches pending, with several Q2 projects moved to Q3 on approval timing; a meaningful part of the 15-20% presales growth guidance depends on these.

Leverage: net debt rose to INR11,900 crore from about INR10,900 crore at March; contingent liabilities rose on corporate guarantees, which management said are mostly SPV-level debt consolidated in group accounts.
Hyderabad mix and realisation: lower realisation (INR8,000-10,000 per sq ft) and about 7 million sq ft of unsold Hyderabad inventory.
Hospitality monetisation: IPO approval expires 30 September; the PE route is unresolved.
Cost inflation from oil and commodity prices, plus a secretarial audit remark on remuneration disclosure that management disputed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the launch pipeline, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly said approvals and RERA delays were the main constraint and that launch dates may move by a quarter or two. Evasive on hospitality monetisation and on specific leasing numbers for BKC and Mahalaxmi.
key_quotes: Business has not got affected because of geopolitics.
We were never, never going to push any launch.
Whatever we are -- INR70,000 crores of revenue we have, it will get recognized in the next 4 years.

adds.what: Chennai Palm Court residential launch (about INR1,200 crore GDV)
Chennai Falcon City (6.84 million sq ft, about INR5,000 crore GDV)
Two annuity projects (Tech Zone and JRC) pushed to around June 2027
Data centre about 100 MW envisaged; no land purchased yet

growth.why: Management reiterated 15-20% presales growth and FY27 residential recognition of INR11,000-12,000 crore, but the Q1 reported residential revenue fell on few completions and launches slipped into Q2/Q3 on approval delays, with backing from a INR45,000 crore pending launch pipeline and a INR70,000 crore unrecognised backlog rather than firm capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Reported EBITDA fell 4% YoY on low handovers and fixed costs ahead of Q2/Q3 launches, though management says project-level margins are unchanged and FY27 resi recognition is guided at INR11,000-12,000 crore, so margins could recover as handovers and launches land.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Four Q1 launches (about 20.16 million sq ft, roughly INR12,000 crore GDV) and three completions totalling 4.37 million sq ft, with Chennai Palm Court in Q2, Falcon City (6.84 million sq ft) in Q3 and Clover Dale (about 4 million sq ft) in Q4, though annuity projects Tech Zone and JRC slipped to around June 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management reiterated 15-20% presales growth, with Q1 resi presales of INR6,579 crore on 337 units and a INR45,000 crore launch pipeline, but a meaningful part of that growth depends on Q2/Q3 launches that are already slipping on approvals.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Data centre of about 100 MW is envisaged with no land bought yet and a Maharashtra land acquisition pending, and BD target is about INR4,500 crore for FY27 with Thane, Borivali and NCR sites added, but no firm capex plan or utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was only held (FCF INR8,500-9,000 crore, BD about INR4,500 crore, FY27 resi recognition INR11,000-12,000 crore) while the current collections run rate implies about INR20,000-21,000 crore against a INR21,000-22,000 crore resi target, leaving no room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Collections guide of INR25,000 crore gross (resi INR21,000-22,000 crore) looks ahead of the current run rate of about INR20,000-21,000 crore, and approval slippage could push Q2/Q3 launches and handovers (about one month delay from labour disruption).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Q2 includes Bangalore (Garden Breez, Avon, Springwood, Battersea), Chennai Palm Court and Park Street; Q3 includes Prestige Meadows (NCR, INR4,500 crore GDV), Bougainvillea Gardens and Chambers 51, all from a INR45,000 crore pipeline, though some approvals may slip into Q3.

rows.label: Unrecognised residential backlog of about INR70,000 crore
rows.why: Backlog of about INR70,000 crore is expected to be recognised over about 4 years, with FY27 residential recognition guided at INR11,000-12,000 crore, supporting revenue visibility even as Q1 reported resi revenue fell to INR1,600 crore.

rows.label: Net debt rising, FCF-funded BD
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR11,900 crore from about INR10,900 crore in March, with FY27 FCF of INR8,500-9,000 crore funding capex and about INR4,500 crore BD, and net debt may rise by at most INR1,000-1,500 crore; Q2/Q3 launches should unlock cash but this is not assured.

rows.label: Hospitality IPO or PE monetisation
rows.why: Hospitality revenue was INR300 crore at about 41% EBITDA margin, and IPO approval expires 30 September with PE interest being explored, but management gave no definitive timeline.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the INR45,000 crore launch pipeline and FY27 guidance, but cautious on approval and RERA timing and evasive on hospitality monetisation; analysts probed the annuity delays, the Q2/Q3 launch slippage and the net debt rise.
